current_behavior: resolve_access looks up denied_commands by command, maps the vector to any(origin.matches(context)), then calls is_some() on the Option. Therefore any deny entry for the command rejects access even when the origin predicate is false.
Denied ResolvedCommand values retain capability window and webview selectors, but resolve_access does not test those selectors before denying.
intended_contract_evidence: Capability documentation describes capabilities as access boundaries for matching windows/webviews and optional remote URL contexts.
Resolved::resolve copies capability context, window patterns, and webview patterns into both allowed_commands and denied_commands.
The allow branch of resolve_access requires both origin and window/webview selector matches.
prepared_controls: allow local/main plus deny remote/main: local/main should remain allowed
allow local/main plus deny local/admin: local/main should remain allowed
allow local/main plus deny local/main: matching deny should still override the allow
candidate: Replace the current map(...).is_some() deny check with is_some_and(...), requiring origin.matches(&cmd.context) and either a matching webview or window pattern, mirroring the allow selector semantics.
execution_status: GitHub Actions scheduling for the temporary carrier could not be made observable through the connected execution surface; do not treat the prepared test as executed.
limitations: resolve_access_message has a separate debug diagnostic branch that also describes any command-level deny as explicit and would need review for message accuracy.
Dynamic capability addition uses the same resolved deny data but was not exercised end to end.
